answer: Yes. The story uses sophisticated metaphor to deepen its uncanny atmosphere and blur the boundaries between people and objects. The woman’s charred-looking silhouette echoes the burned chair, suggesting an unresolved connection between them. Comparisons such as the power failing “like someone walking through a house closing doors” turn ordinary events into ominous, intimate gestures. The idiom “a word on the tip of my tongue,” extended into “as if they were a name I had once known,” also establishes the narrator’s unsettling sense of recognition.
